description:
Cookie-cutter sweep to migrate every Value-typed field whose semantic is 'PatchObject' (RFC 8620 §5.3) to the typed jmap_types::PatchObject newtype, across the 7 extension-types crates.

## Background

The PatchObject newtype landed in jmap-types via JMAP-o7cj (2026-05-08). Subsequent adoption epics (JMAP-wrgs calendars, JMAP-6h5s mail, JMAP-zk6m chat+contacts+filenode+sharing+tasks) migrated /set request paths and SetObject::Patch associated types — but DELIBERATELY excluded fields that were *nested-map* patches (Pattern β: Option<HashMap<K, V>>) or *notification-payload* patches (Pattern α: Option<V>) because those are not /set arguments.

3 follow-up beads (JMAP-78lb, JMAP-s0p5, JMAP-pmpa) were filed for 3 of those leftover sites. A workspace survey on 2026-05-09 (after the user reminded me about the canonical-template propagation rule replacing LOCKED) found 5 MORE leftover sites the original 3 beads did not cover, plus 1 cross-cutting key-type inconsistency. This epic is the proper container for the full sweep.

## Survey results — 8 fields + 1 key-type dimension

### Pattern α (top-level Option<Value> → Option<PatchObject>)

  1. calendars-types  src/notification.rs:99   CalendarEventNotification::event_patch  [JMAP-pmpa]
  2. tasks-types      src/notification.rs:88   TaskNotification::task_patch            [JMAP-s0p5]

### Pattern β (nested-map Option<HashMap<K, Value>> → Option<HashMap<K, PatchObject>>)

  3. mail-types       src/mdn.rs:231           MdnSendRequest::on_success_update_email [JMAP-78lb]
  4. tasks-types      src/task.rs:323          Task::recurrence_overrides              (newly surfaced)
  5. tasks-types      src/task.rs:375          Task::localizations                     (newly surfaced)

### Pattern β with shape change (currently α-shaped Option<Value>; doc says β-shaped — workspace divergence)

  6. calendars-types  src/event.rs:193         CalendarEvent::recurrence_overrides     (newly surfaced)
  7. calendars-types  src/event.rs:240         CalendarEvent::localizations            (newly surfaced)
  8. contacts-types   src/card.rs:155          ContactCard::localizations              (newly surfaced)

### Cross-cutting key-type fix (cookie-cutter inconsistency vs client-side)

  9. mail-types       src/mdn.rs:231           MdnSendRequest::on_success_update_email key type: HashMap<String, _> → HashMap<Id, _> (matches mail-client/src/methods/submission.rs::EmailSubmissionSetParams)

## Cookie-cutter analysis

Before this sweep, 3 sister crates have inconsistent shapes for 'recurrenceOverrides' / 'localizations':
- tasks-types:     Option<HashMap<String, Value>>   (already β)
- calendars-types: Option<Value>                    (α-shaped — divergent)
- contacts-types:  Option<Value>                    (α-shaped — divergent, only has localizations)

Tasks-types defines the canonical shape for the family: Option<HashMap<String, PatchObject>>. The sweep both tightens the value type AND unifies the outer shape across the 3 sister crates.

## Acceptance criteria for the epic

- All 8 + 1 sites migrated.
- 'cargo test --workspace --all-features' green.
- 'cargo clippy --workspace --lib --all-features -- -D warnings' clean.
- Wire format byte-identical (PatchObject is #[serde(transparent)]; Id is #[serde(transparent)]).
- Per-crate PLAN.md updated where the field's row references the new typed shape.
- 'diff -u' between sister types crates shows only RFC content differences in the affected fields, no shape differences.

## Out of scope (separate cleanups)

- MdnSendResponse::not_sent (Option<HashMap<String, Value>>): values are SetError, not PatchObject. Belongs to a future SetError-relocation epic.
- JSCalendar / JSContact sub-object fields (~30+ fields across calendars/tasks/contacts types): documented Sloppy-Value carriers per workspace AGENTS.md; explicitly OUT of scope.

## Decomposition

One child bead per (crate, field). 9 children total. Each child closes when its specific field has migrated and gates pass. Existing 3 beads (JMAP-78lb, JMAP-s0p5, JMAP-pmpa) become children of this epic. 6 new children get filed.

## Why decompose first

User instruction (2026-05-09): scope was wider than originally beaded (3 known → 8 actual + 1 key-type). Decomposing into a proper epic with all child beads filed BEFORE writing any code lets the user review the full scope and approve/decline per-field if needed. Avoids the mistake of treating 'approve-all-3' as authorization for a wider sweep that wasn't yet visible at decision time.
notes: Filed 2026-05-09 after user correction reminding agent that LOCKED framing was replaced by canonical-template propagation rule (memory: locked-superseded-by-canonical-template). Survey methodology: rg for Option<serde_json::Value>, Option<HashMap<*, Value>>, and the literal 'PatchObject' across all 7 extension-types crates; cross-checked doc-comments and per-crate PLAN.md to classify Sloppy-Value (stay) vs PatchObject (migrate). PatchObject is #[serde(transparent)] over Map<String, Value> with private inner; construction is via PatchObject::from_map(map) or Map::into(); read-side is patch.as_map() or patch.into_inner().
title: EPIC: PatchObject typed-envelope sweep across extension-types (cookie-cutter)
